A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Priority-Aware Shapley Value work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the expanded appendix structure.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix B report original data-valuation experiments on MNIST/CIFAR10 and feature-attribution experiments on Census Income, including repeated-run results.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by synthetic mixing and estimation studies in Appendix D and DAG-perturbation experiments in Appendix F.4.2.

M1.justification: The PASV distribution and original adjacent-swap sampler remain unchanged. Section 6.1 and Appendix D.2 add an optional estimation procedure combining a fitted quadratic utility proxy, pairwise-order probabilities and Monte Carlo residual correction. New Algorithm 2 also computes exact stationary pairwise probabilities through weighted dynamic programming.

E1.justification: v2 adds four synthetic poset families and sum-of-unanimity games under block-based and ordered-partition precedence structures. It also evaluates locally perturbed and disconnected Census Income DAGs. The original MNIST, CIFAR10 and Census Income application coverage remains.

E2.justification: The original SV, WSV and PSV comparator sets are unchanged. The new proxy-estimation experiment compares against direct Monte Carlo and includes a linear-only proxy alongside quadratic variants (Figure 10). Regression MSR and PolySHAP inform the adaptation but are not separately benchmarked.

E3.justification: The original application settings are retained. Appendix D introduces separate mixing, approximation-error and computational-cost protocols, including exact stationary references, ARE/AUCC metrics, player counts up to 8192 and controlled proxy budgets. Appendix F.4.2 adds specified edge-deletion, addition, cut and top-K tests with attribution and order-change metrics.

E4.justification: v2 retains the original priority sweeps and adds sampler-mixing analysis, estimation-error convergence, quadratic-term and fitting-budget ablations, and runtime/memory scaling. The new DAG-misspecification study tests local edge changes, disconnections and influential-edge subsets, substantially extending robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1.1 newly specifies 10,000 independent chains per mixing condition. The original application studies retain ten estimation seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. No new confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical numerical results. New Figures 8–12 report mixing, approximation error, runtime and memory outcomes, including conditional benefits from the proxy estimator. Figure 19 adds DAG-sensitivity findings: most individual perturbations have small effects, while deleting marital-status→relationship produces an attribution shift of approximately 0.32.

T1.justification: v1 states the central theoretical results without their proofs. New Appendices B–C supply proofs for the axiomatization theorems, reduction propositions, limiting-weight propositions and acceptance-ratio lemma, together with auxiliary lemmas. Appendix D additionally develops weighted recursions and analytical expressions for benchmark and proxy values.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: combining hard precedence with soft weights, recovering existing values, axiomatic characterization, scalable MCMC and priority sweeping. The added evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendices D/F add substantive applicability qualifications: utility evaluation versus sampling costs, dependence of proxy benefits on utility structure and fitting budget, and substantial memory overhead. They also explain why consequential DAG changes should alter attribution and frame edge sensitivity as guidance for validating the assumed graph.

D1.justification: v2 documents synthetic graph and utility construction, weighted dynamic programming, utility caching, simulation sampling settings, proxy/probability budgets and explicit perturbation edge lists. Runtime and memory measurements are newly provided. Existing generative-model and feature-classifier implementation details are retained in Appendices E–F.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused connections to Regression MSR, PolySHAP and regression-based KernelSHAP, plus references supporting poset counting, mixing experiments, synthetic benchmarks and the ROV proof. The original positioning of PASV relative to PSV and WSV remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains essentially verbatim. v2 inserts a computational-cost/DAG-sensitivity section and dedicated proof/simulation appendices, separates the former experimental appendix into E and F, and updates headings, cross-references and the publication footer.

P2.justification: v2 adds six substantial multipanel figures covering mixing, estimation accuracy, runtime, memory and DAG sensitivity, together with an algorithm box and perturbation edge tables. Existing figures and numerical tables are retained; appendix figures are renumbered and some image grids are resized and reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves auditability by supplying previously missing proofs and controlled evidence on computational scaling, estimator tradeoffs and local DAG misspecification. The new cost and memory results also make practical limitations clearer. These gains outweigh a dropped common factor in Appendix B.1's intermediate limit, which cancels after normalization, and optimistic wording about obtaining small errors from a few hundred permutations relative to Figure 9.
